parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-31, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 2792.1 | 0.92 | 0.92
2 | 1847.0 | 0.49 | 1.41
3 | 2743.7 | 1.01 | 2.42
4 | 1318.3 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-31, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Groundwater Site Note: Station T-31 (Survey Area T)**

**Layer Sequence Summary:**
- **Layer 1 (0.00–0.92 m):** High-resistivity surface layer ($2792.1\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness: $0.92\text{ m}$).
- **Layer 2 (0.92–1.41 m):** Intermediate lower-resistivity zone ($1847.0\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness: $0.49\text{ m}$).
- **Layer 3 (1.41–2.42 m):** Resistive layer ($2743.7\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$, thickness: $1.01\text{ m}$).
- **Layer 4 (>2.42 m):** Basal low-resistivity zone ($1318.3\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$).

**Curve Type Verification:**
The resistivity sequence across layers 1–2–3 decreases then increases ($\rho_1 > \rho_2 < \rho_3$), forming an **H** segment. Across layers 2–3–4, resistivity increases then decreases ($\rho_2 < \rho_3 > \rho_4$), forming a **K** segment. The resulting 4-layer sounding corresponds correctly to an **HK**-type curve, matching the classification on file.

{"curve_type_stated": "HK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
